ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a nitrogen-containing six-membered ring connected to a fused saturated bridged ring/bicyclic fragment on the left side, with a chiral center indicated by a wedge-shaped bond at the upper left. On the right side of the six-membered ring there is a hydrogen labeled H, with a base :B beside it, and a curved arrow from :B pointing to this H. Another arrow indicates that the C-H bond electrons enter the ring to form a new double bond; there is also an arrow from the bond between the ring carbon and the external pyrrolidine nitrogen pointing to the pyrrolidine nitrogen, indicating that this C-N bond breaks and pushes the electrons to nitrogen. Reasoning: After the arrow pushing, the base removes the indicated hydrogen, the C-H bond electrons fill into the ring to form the missing double bond, and at the same time the external pyrrolidine substituent leaves from the ring; the fused saturated skeleton on the left side remains unchanged, and the wedge-shaped chiral center is also retained. Therefore, the product is a fused bicyclic aza-diene/imine skeleton, corresponding to the SMILES [C@H]1(C2)CCC2C3=CC=NC=C13.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image first and map the atoms around the six-membered N-containing ring and fused bicyclic fragment. Follow the arrows: base :B removes the indicated H, the C-H electrons form the missing double bond in the ring, and the bond from the ring carbon to the pyrrolidine N is pushed onto N, disconnecting the pyrrolidine substituent. Keep the fused saturated cage unchanged and preserve the stereocenter shown by the wedge. The remaining product skeleton is the fused bicyclic aza-diene/imine framework, which is written as [C@H]1(C2)CCC2C3=CC=NC=C13.

method.method_draft: Treat the diagram as a base-promoted aromatizing/eliminating electron relocation.
